afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 111957
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
1257 PM MST Wed Nov 11 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- High pressure will continue to maintain dry and tranquil conditions
  and above normal temperatures in place through Thursday.

- A more unsettled pattern is expected starting Friday and lasting
  well into next week with occasional rain chances and cooler 
  temperatures.
  
&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Latest objective analysis continues to depict upper-level ridging 
persisting over the Desert Southwest. This ridge will remain in 
place through much of Thursday before shifting east late Thursday
night into early Friday as a shortwave trough approaches from the
west. In the meantime, dry and tranquil weather along with mostly
clear skies will remain in place through Thursday. Temperatures 
will also continue to run about 5 degrees above normal as 
afternoon highs top out in the low to mid 80s across much of the 
lower desert communities with overnight and early morning lows 
remaining mild with 50s to around 60 degrees expected.

&&

.LONG TERM /FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
Model guidance continues to show a significant pattern change
starting Thursday and eventually affecting our region by Friday,
but a decent amount of spread and uncertainty remains with any
rain potential for the first two shortwaves that will brush by our
area. The leading shortwave is still slated to approach southern
California by Friday morning, but the track should keep the best
energy across northern Baja and Sonora Mexico. The system will at
least advect a decent amount of moisture into the region later
Thursday into Friday pushing PWATs to around 200% of normal by
Friday afternoon. Lower level moisture will noticeably improve
during this time, but mixing ratios will only top out at 6-7 g/kg.  

There is at least some improved optimism for rain chances as
models have mostly kept the track of the system not too far away
on Friday with the weakening circulation moving along or just
south of the Arizona/Mexico border. This track along with the
modest moisture should at least allow for around a 12 hour period
of rain chances from later Friday morning through mid to late
evening Friday. The best focus for the expected shower activity
(and maybe a weak thunderstorm or two) should be south of Phoenix
earlier Friday before shifting east of Phoenix by the evening. 
Forecast PoPs have increased to include 25-40% chances in the 
Phoenix area to 50-70% over the high terrain northeast and east of
Phoenix. Rainfall amounts with this first round of rain chances 
should only amount to a few hundredths for any the lower deserts 
to at maybe 0.10" in higher terrain areas. 

A second follow-on shortwave trough is then shown to quickly move
in from the northwest as early as sunrise Saturday morning,
lasting through at least Saturday afternoon. The track of this
next disturbance will at least bring rain chances to the northern
half of Arizona with more doubt for the Arizona lower deserts. The
latest NBM PoPs of 40-70% for Phoenix and 60-90% for the high
terrain seem too optimistic, but have held off on making any 
adjustments at this time. Rainfall amounts for Saturday should at
least be higher than the first round with forecast soundings
pointing at a near saturated mid-level layer, but with a less 
favorable upslope west southwest wind component we'll have to 
mostly rely on system dynamics for forcing. 

By Saturday evening, the shortwave is expected to push to our
east quickly decreasing rain chances and likely ending them all
together by around midnight. Sunday will bring brief shortwave
ridging and some slight dry air advection from the northwest and
this should lead to considerably less clouds and virtually no 
rain chances. Temperatures this weekend will easily fall into the 
70s for highs with most lower deserts likely not surpassing 75 
degrees both days.

The high amplitude unsettled weather pattern will continue into
next week, but model uncertainty increases even more. Guidance
suggests one after another northern Pacific waves will get 
ejected southeastward toward the U.S. West Coast with the next
potential system reaching the California coast early Monday before
reaching our region Monday night into Tuesday. This may even be 
followed by another system during the second half of next week. It
is too early to have any good sense on the track of these systems
as they could move directly through the Desert Southwest or 
mostly miss us to the north. NBM/WPC PoPs of 20-60% are still in 
the forecast for the Tuesday disturbance, but that could easily 
change depending on the eventual track. So far, any system that 
may move through is not expected to carry anything more than 
average moisture, so any rainfall amounts are likely to be on the 
lighter side. However, the expected northwestward trajectory of 
the weather systems next week should usher in even cooler 
temperatures with highs trending more toward the upper 60s to 
lower 70s during the middle part of the week. 

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 1715Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT:
No major aviation concerns are expected during the TAF period
under mostly clear skies. Winds will favor an E'rly component
through much of the period with speeds generally aob 10 kt. Though
VRB conditions may yield some W'rly observations this afternoon,
the typical full diurnal switch appears unlikely to take place. A
short window of marginal breeziness may develop late in the
forecast, but any gusts that come to fruition should quickly 
diminish soon after.

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:
No major weather concerns are expected over the next 24 hours.
Winds will continue to favor a W'rly component at KIPL, while KBLH
switches between NE and NW flow. Speeds generally aob 7 kt will
yield extended periods of VRB conditions. Mostly clear skies will
be common through Thursday morning. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
The dry conditions and above normal temperatures will persist
through Thursday before chances for mostly light rain begin 
Friday. Minimum humidity values through Thursday will range
between 20-30% for the lower deserts to 30-40% for higher terrain
areas, while overnight recoveries stay good to excellent at 
40-70%. Expect overall light winds, but also some marginally 
breezy conditions across ridge tops and terrain gaps of eastern 
districts during the morning hours. Winds will increase starting
Friday, but gusts should mostly stay under 25 mph. Several passing
weak weather disturbances will bring occasional showers and maybe
an isolated thunderstorm Friday and Saturday and potentially again
early next week. 

&&

.HYDROLOGY...

Gila: A Flood Warning remains in effect from Painted Rock Dam 
through the Dateland area through at least early next week due to 
water released from the dam. Water release levels are expected to 
increase during the next couple of days, peaking at 3000 cfs. 
These increased releases will have the potential to flood farm 
fields and low-water crossings along the river downstream from the
dam.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...None.
CA...None.
&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Lojero
LONG TERM...Kuhlman 
AVIATION...RW 
FIRE WEATHER...Kuhlman 
HYDROLOGY...Lojero
